units.translation: ⟦1⟧ the same at 1013 there; Orestes refers back to this scene of the Choephori with 461. ⟦2⟧ in the technical sense of testimony from an absent person or about hearsay is even less possible to take here than ⟦3⟧; it is nothing but a strengthening of ⟦4⟧ (this of the same thing ⟦5⟧), and Paley correctly compares ⟦6⟧ N.: ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧. –
for to bear witness about one's own fortunes to all is foolish
but to conceal them is wise

465 ff. The scholiast correctly recalls 426. There is nothing to object to in ⟦1⟧ (Homer A 335), except that it already recurs at 467 (⟦2⟧) in the same position; so there the conjecture ⟦3⟧ (cf. 199) improves it, which at the same time brings out more sharply the different sense in 465 and 467. No offense is naturally to be taken at the pleonasm ⟦4⟧.
⟦1⟧ cf. 136; on the matter ⟦2⟧ 1030 ff. In 467 v. Wilamowitz writes well ⟦3⟧, cf. ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧.
I would drive away, I would keep off
if anything of this prelude goes astray
but if you will do any of these things
having done this in every way in you, I will be content
in every way you will be good
in every way we will try to be good
or we, acting as friends to you in every way
⟦1⟧ to ⟦2⟧. With this both parties have submitted to Athena's judgment, even if the Erinyes not so unconditionally as Orestes.

⟦1⟧: for ⟦2⟧ is in any case necessary; for for ⟦3⟧ it would have to be ⟦4⟧ or ⟦5⟧. But whether ⟦6⟧ or ⟦7⟧, that can be disputed. With ⟦8⟧ human judges are immediately thought of, and these are then somewhat rejected, which does not fit with what follows 483 ff.; with ⟦9⟧ one thinks of Orestes' words 468, and Athena thus first raises two objections against a decision by herself: the first not yet serious, but the second introduced by ⟦10⟧? for me it is (as a goddess) not in accordance with sacred right (on ⟦11⟧ mostly emphasis) to judge in a blood matter, since this is the affair of the punishing deities (the Erinyes), see the chorus 360 ff.
⟦1⟧ is not to be changed into -⟦2⟧; for of the ⟦3⟧ for the ⟦4⟧ there is talk only from 477 ff.
of sharp wrath, of bitter anger
